pointers.sentence: So `SimpleTestCase`, the base of every Django test case class, does its own work around each test from `__call__`, the method `unittest` calls to run one: its docstring says this is so that a project's test case need not call `super().setUp()` (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.__call__`).
`unittest`'s suite calls a test with the result that collects outcomes, and `__call__` passes that to `SimpleTestCase._setup_and_call` (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._setup_and_call`):

ShipNumberTests' method never ran: on a database with transactions, `TestCase._fixture_setup`, which `_pre_setup` calls, refuses `TransactionTestCase.reset_sequences` (`django/test/testcases.py:TestCase._fixture_setup`).

`django/test/testcases.py` sets `__unittest = True`, the mark of a module whose frames `unittest` cuts from a reported traceback: those it starts with, and, in a failure, every frame from the next of them on.
So a failure in one of Django's assertions is reported without the assertion's frames: easier to read, the release note says, and `--pdb` enters the failing test directly (`docs/releases/5.2.txt`).

`SimpleTestCase.debug` runs the same steps but raises what they would add to a result, and runs the test by `unittest.TestCase.debug`, so a failing test never reaches `_post_teardown` (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.debug`).

`SimpleTestCase._pre_setup` makes a test client and an asynchronous one, of the classes `SimpleTestCase.client_class` and `SimpleTestCase.async_client_class` name, and empties the local-memory email backend's outbox (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._pre_setup`).
A project's `setUpClass` that does not call the parent's loses all of this, as the documentation warns (`docs/topics/testing/tools.txt`).

`SimpleTestCase.assertRaisesMessage` and `SimpleTestCase.assertWarnsMessage` are `unittest.TestCase.assertRaises` and `unittest.TestCase.assertWarns` with a check that the expected text is in the string of what was caught, as a substring, not a pattern (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._assert_raises_or_warns_cm`).
Given a callable and its arguments, the assertion calls it; given none, it is a context manager (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._assertFooMessage`).

Each valid input must clean to its value in both, each invalid one raise a `ValidationError` with the messages given, and each of `empty_values` be refused by the first with its `"required"` message and cleaned by the second to the empty value given, `""` by default; a subclass of `django.forms.fields.CharField` must accept `min_length=2` and `max_length=20` (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.assertFieldOutput`).
